sourceNote: Original supplemental classroom practice. Teacher review recommended. Not official state standards questions.

questions.clue: What is 25% of 80?
questions.why: One quarter of 80 is 20.

questions.clue: What is the product of 9 and 7?
questions.why: 9 multiplied by 7 is 63.

questions.clue: A square has side length 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.why: Four sides of 6 cm total 24 cm.

questions.clue: Which fraction equals 0.75?
questions.why: 0.75 is 75/100, which simplifies to 3/4.

questions.clue: What is 3/5 of 45?
questions.why: 45 divided by 5 and multiplied by 3 is 27.

questions.clue: A triangle has base 10 and height 6. What is its area?
questions.why: Triangle area is one half times base times height.

questions.clue: Solve 4x + 6 = 30.
questions.why: Subtract 6 and divide 24 by 4.

questions.clue: What is the mean of 5, 7, 10, and 14?
questions.why: The sum is 36; divide by four values.

questions.clue: A $48 item is discounted by 25%. What is the sale price?
questions.why: A 25% discount is $12, leaving $36.

questions.clue: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. How long is the hypotenuse?
questions.why: The Pythagorean theorem gives √(25 + 144) = 13.

questions.clue: What is 2 to the fifth power?
questions.why: Multiply five factors of 2 together.

questions.clue: What is the probability of rolling an even number on a fair six-sided die?
questions.why: Three of six faces are even.

questions.clue: A car travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.why: Divide distance by elapsed time.

questions.clue: The pattern 3, 7, 11, 15 follows which rule?
questions.why: Each term increases by four.

questions.clue: What is the volume of a rectangular prism 4 by 5 by 8 units?
questions.why: Multiply the three dimensions.

questions.clue: Which force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.why: Gravity attracts masses toward one another.

questions.clue: What is the process of liquid water changing into gas?
questions.why: Evaporation is the liquid-to-gas change.

questions.clue: Which organ pumps blood through the human body?
questions.why: The heart drives circulation.

questions.clue: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.why: Cells are the smallest structural units of living things.

questions.clue: In a food chain, what is a plant usually classified as?
questions.why: Plants use sunlight to make their own food.

questions.clue: What type of energy is stored in a stretched rubber band?
questions.why: Stretching stores potential energy in the material.

questions.clue: A substance with pH 3 is generally classified as what?
questions.why: Solutions below pH 7 are acidic.

questions.clue: Which part of an atom has a negative electric charge?
questions.why: An electron carries negative charge.

questions.clue: When a surface rubs against another, which force opposes sliding?
questions.why: Friction resists relative movement of surfaces.

questions.clue: Why does a sealed syringe of air resist being compressed?
questions.answer: Gas particles move closer together and pressure rises
questions.why: Compression reduces volume and raises gas pressure.

questions.clue: Which is a chemical change?
questions.why: Rusting produces a new chemical substance.

questions.clue: A circuit with a broken wire is described as what?
questions.why: An open circuit does not form a complete conducting path.

questions.clue: When mass stays constant, doubling net force does what to acceleration?
questions.why: Newton's second law gives a = F/m.

questions.clue: Which is evidence of a controlled experiment?
questions.answer: Only one independent variable is deliberately changed
questions.why: Changing one factor helps isolate causal effects.

questions.clue: When energy transfers from a warmer object to a cooler object, that transfer is called what?
questions.why: Heat is energy transferred due to a temperature difference.

questions.clue: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.why: Iron oxide helps give Mars its reddish appearance.

questions.clue: What causes daytime and nighttime on Earth?
questions.why: Rotation changes which hemisphere faces the Sun.

questions.clue: Which object is at the center of our solar system?
questions.why: Planets orbit the Sun.

questions.clue: What kind of rock forms when lava cools?
questions.why: Cooled magma or lava forms igneous rock.

questions.clue: Which atmospheric layer has most everyday weather?
questions.why: Most clouds and weather develop in the troposphere.

questions.clue: What is the name for Earth's natural satellite?
questions.why: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

questions.clue: Which tectonic boundary involves plates moving apart?
questions.why: Divergent boundaries separate and can form new crust.

questions.clue: What term describes a huge rotating storm over warm tropical oceans?
questions.why: Tropical cyclones draw energy from warm ocean waters.

questions.clue: Why do we experience seasons?
questions.answer: Earth's axis is tilted relative to its orbit
wrong: Earth is much closer to the Sun in summer
questions.why: Tilt changes Sun angle and daylight duration.

questions.clue: Which instrument detects seismic waves from earthquakes?
questions.why: A seismometer records ground motion.

questions.clue: Which process carries sediment away from a hillside?
questions.why: Erosion removes and transports weathered materials.

questions.clue: What mainly drives ocean surface tides?
questions.answer: Gravity from the Moon, with a contribution from the Sun
questions.why: Lunar and solar gravity create tidal forces.

questions.clue: If a star's light shifts toward longer wavelengths due to motion away, what is that called?
questions.why: Receding light sources exhibit Doppler redshift.

questions.clue: What makes a scientific climate trend different from one day's weather?
questions.answer: It describes patterns over long periods
questions.why: Climate is a long-term pattern of weather conditions.

questions.clue: Where is new oceanic crust commonly formed?
questions.why: Seafloor spreading creates crust at divergent ridges.

questions.clue: Which document begins with 'We the People'?
questions.why: The Constitution's preamble starts with that phrase.

questions.clue: What branch of the U.S. government interprets federal law?
questions.why: Federal courts are in the judicial branch.

questions.clue: Which explorer led the first expedition to circumnavigate Earth, although he died before it ended?
questions.why: Magellan led the expedition; Juan Sebastián Elcano completed it.

questions.clue: What is the purpose of checks and balances?
questions.why: Each branch can restrain actions of the others.

questions.clue: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids at Giza?
questions.why: Giza's large pyramids are monuments of ancient Egypt.

questions.clue: What do citizens usually do in a representative democracy?
questions.why: Representatives act on behalf of voters.

questions.clue: Which event began in 1775 and led to U.S. independence?
questions.why: The Revolutionary War began in 1775.

questions.clue: What did the 19th Amendment prohibit denying on the basis of sex?
questions.why: The amendment protected voting rights regardless of sex.

questions.clue: Which empire was centered in the city of Rome?
questions.why: The Roman Empire grew from the city of Rome.

questions.clue: What system divides power between national and state governments?
questions.why: Federalism shares governing authority across levels.

questions.clue: What did the U.S. Civil War end with in 1865?
questions.why: Major Confederate armies surrendered in 1865.

questions.clue: What is a primary historical source?
questions.answer: A diary written during an event
wrong: A documentary made a century later
questions.why: Primary sources originate from the period or participants studied.

questions.clue: Which Supreme Court case declared segregated public schools unconstitutional in 1954?
questions.why: Brown rejected racial segregation in public education.

questions.clue: What is the purpose of a constitutional amendment?
questions.answer: Change the Constitution through its formal process
questions.why: Amendments alter the nation's foundational legal framework.

questions.clue: Why do historians compare multiple accounts of the same event?
questions.answer: To identify perspectives and corroborate evidence
questions.why: Comparison can reveal agreement, conflict, and source limitations.

questions.clue: Which word is a synonym of 'rapid'?
questions.why: Rapid and fast both describe speed.

questions.clue: Which punctuation mark usually ends a direct question?
questions.why: A question mark indicates direct inquiry.

questions.clue: What is the plural of 'mouse' when referring to animals?
questions.why: The irregular plural is mice.

questions.clue: Which prefix means 'again'?
questions.why: Re- indicates repetition, as in rewrite.

questions.clue: In 'The bright lantern glowed,' which word is an adjective?
questions.why: Bright describes the noun lantern.

questions.clue: Which word means the opposite of 'scarce'?
questions.why: Abundant describes a large supply.

questions.clue: What is the main purpose of a topic sentence?
questions.why: A topic sentence introduces the paragraph's main point.

questions.clue: Which word uses a root meaning 'life'?
questions.why: Bio- comes from a root meaning life.

questions.clue: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.why: A singular possessive noun takes apostrophe-s.

questions.clue: What literary device compares things using 'like' or 'as'?
questions.why: A simile uses an explicit comparison.

questions.clue: What is an inference?
questions.answer: A conclusion drawn from evidence and reasoning
wrong: An unsupported guess stated as fact
questions.why: Inference uses clues to reason beyond stated details.

questions.clue: Which source is strongest for checking a current scientific claim?
questions.why: Scientific review and methodology help assess claims.

questions.clue: Which sentence has a dependent clause?
questions.why: 'Although it rained' cannot stand alone.

questions.clue: What is the author's tone?
questions.answer: The attitude conveyed toward the subject
questions.why: Tone is the attitude suggested by word choice and style.

questions.clue: Which technique strengthens an argument most?
questions.why: Evidence tied to the claim makes reasoning stronger.

questions.clue: What does a computer keyboard mainly provide?
questions.why: A keyboard sends input to a device.

questions.clue: What is a strong password practice?
questions.why: Long unique credentials reduce risk of compromise.

questions.clue: Which device displays a computer's visual output?
questions.why: A monitor shows visual output.

questions.clue: What does a URL help identify?
questions.answer: The address of a web resource
questions.why: A URL locates a resource on the web.

questions.clue: Why should you check an article's publication date?
questions.why: Some facts and claims change over time.

questions.clue: What is a spreadsheet cell?
questions.answer: One intersection of a row and column
questions.why: Cells store values or formulas in tables.

questions.clue: What does 'phishing' usually involve?
questions.why: Phishing impersonates trust to steal data or access.

questions.clue: What is an algorithm?
questions.answer: A defined sequence of steps for a task
questions.why: Algorithms specify processes or computations.

questions.clue: Why use alt text for meaningful images?
questions.answer: Improve accessibility for screen reader users
questions.why: Alt text communicates important visual meaning.

questions.clue: What does a conditional statement do in programming?
questions.answer: Chooses an action based on a condition
questions.why: Conditionals branch based on whether conditions hold.

questions.clue: Which file format commonly stores structured data as key-value pairs?
questions.why: JSON represents structured data with objects and arrays.

questions.clue: What is two-factor authentication?
questions.why: Multi-factor authentication uses distinct factor types.

questions.clue: What is one limitation of a biased training data set?
questions.answer: A model may produce systematically unfair results
questions.why: Biased data can yield biased outputs.

questions.clue: What does a Git commit record?
questions.answer: A snapshot of changes and associated metadata
questions.why: Commits preserve versioned changes.

questions.clue: What is the key difference between correlation and causation?
questions.answer: Correlation alone does not establish cause
wrong: They always mean the same thing
questions.why: A relationship does not by itself establish why it occurs.

questions.clue: Solve 3x - 7 = 11.
questions.why: Add 7 then divide by 3.

questions.clue: What is the slope of y = -2x + 5?
questions.why: Slope is the coefficient of x.

questions.clue: What is the area of a circle with radius 3?
questions.why: Area is πr².

questions.clue: Simplify (x + 2)(x + 3).
questions.why: Distribute both binomials.

questions.clue: For f(x) = x² - 4, what is f(3)?
questions.why: 3 squared minus 4 equals 5.

questions.clue: A line has slope 3 and y-intercept -4. What is its equation?
questions.why: Slope-intercept form is y = mx + b.

questions.clue: Solve x² - 9 = 0.
questions.why: Both positive and negative 3 square to 9.

questions.clue: What is the distance between (0,0) and (6,8)?
questions.why: The distance formula gives √(36+64).

questions.clue: Which transformation preserves both angles and distances?
questions.why: A translation is a rigid motion.

questions.clue: What is the discriminant of x² - 4x + 4 = 0?
Simplify log10(1000).
questions.why: 10 cubed equals 1000.

questions.clue: If two similar triangles have side ratio 2:3, what is their area ratio?
questions.why: Area scales with the square of side lengths.

questions.clue: Solve the system x+y=7 and x-y=1.
questions.why: Adding equations gives 2x=8.

questions.clue: What is the vertex of y = (x - 2)² + 5?
questions.why: Vertex form is y=a(x-h)²+k.

questions.clue: If sin θ = 3/5 in a right triangle, which ratio is sin θ?
questions.why: Sine compares the opposite side to the hypotenuse.

questions.clue: What is the atomic number of carbon?
questions.why: Carbon has six protons.

questions.clue: Which particle has a positive electric charge?
questions.why: Protons carry positive charge.

questions.clue: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.why: Each water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.clue: A neutral atom has 8 protons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.why: Neutral atoms have equal positive and negative charge.

questions.clue: Which element uses symbol Na?
questions.why: Na comes from natrium, Latin for sodium.

questions.clue: What is the approximate pH of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.why: Neutral water is around pH 7 at this temperature.

questions.clue: What type of bond involves sharing pairs of electrons?
questions.why: Covalent bonds share electrons.

questions.clue: What is a mole used to count in chemistry?
questions.why: One mole contains Avogadro's number of entities.

questions.clue: Which principle says atoms are conserved in ordinary chemical reactions?
questions.why: Chemical reactions rearrange atoms rather than creating them.

questions.clue: What is the molar mass of H₂O, using H≈1 and O≈16?
questions.why: Two H atoms and one O atom yield about 18 g/mol.

questions.clue: Which reaction generally releases thermal energy to surroundings?
questions.why: An exothermic process transfers heat out.

questions.clue: What does a catalyst typically do?
questions.answer: Lower activation energy without being consumed overall
questions.why: A catalyst offers an alternate reaction pathway.

questions.clue: In a balanced chemical equation, coefficients represent what?
questions.why: Balanced coefficients give stoichiometric ratios.

questions.clue: For N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, how many moles of H₂ react with 2 moles of N₂?
questions.why: The reaction needs three H₂ for each N₂.

questions.clue: Which property primarily determines an element's identity?
questions.why: Atomic number is the proton count.

questions.clue: Which organelle is the main site of photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.why: Chloroplasts contain photosynthetic machinery.

questions.clue: What molecule carries genetic instructions in most organisms?
questions.why: DNA stores inherited instructions.

questions.clue: Which body system transports oxygen in the blood?
questions.why: Blood circulation distributes oxygen.

questions.clue: What is the functional unit of heredity?
questions.why: Genes are hereditary DNA segments.

questions.clue: Which process divides one cell into two genetically similar daughter cells?
questions.why: Mitosis segregates duplicated chromosomes.

questions.clue: What does a population mean in ecology?
questions.answer: Members of one species in a particular area
questions.why: A population groups members of the same species.

questions.clue: What molecule do cells use as a common immediate energy carrier?
questions.why: ATP transfers energy for cellular work.

questions.clue: What is the role of ribosomes?
questions.why: Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptides.

questions.clue: In a simple dominant/recessive trait, what is a heterozygous genotype?
questions.why: Heterozygous means two different alleles.

questions.clue: In natural selection, which trait tends to become more common?
questions.answer: A heritable trait that improves reproductive success
questions.why: Selection changes frequencies when inherited traits affect reproduction.

questions.clue: What is homeostasis?
questions.why: Feedback systems help regulate internal variables.

questions.clue: Why are decomposers important?
questions.answer: They recycle nutrients from dead matter
questions.why: Decomposition returns nutrients to ecosystems.

questions.clue: What is the usual direction of information flow in the central dogma?
questions.why: Gene expression generally transcribes DNA and translates RNA.

questions.clue: If Aa and Aa parents cross, what fraction of offspring genotypes is aa in a simple Mendelian model?
questions.why: Punnett-square combinations AA, Aa, Aa, aa give one aa in four.

questions.clue: What is the main source of energy for most terrestrial food webs?
questions.why: Photosynthesis captures sunlight into chemical energy.

questions.clue: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.why: Force is measured in newtons.

questions.clue: What does speed measure?
questions.why: Speed compares path length with elapsed time.

questions.clue: A stationary object has what velocity relative to the ground?
questions.why: No change in position means zero velocity.

questions.clue: What is the unit of electric current?
questions.why: Current is measured in amperes.

questions.clue: A 2 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s². What net force acts on it?
What is power in physics?
questions.why: Power describes the rate of energy transfer.

questions.clue: If a 12 V source is across a 4 Ω resistor, what current flows?
questions.why: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 3 A.

questions.clue: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving at 4 m/s?
questions.why: Kinetic energy is ½mv².

questions.clue: What is the approximate acceleration of free fall near Earth's surface?
questions.why: Near surface g is about 9.8 m/s² downward.

questions.clue: What is the momentum of a 5 kg mass moving at 3 m/s?
questions.why: Linear momentum is mass times velocity.

questions.clue: If work is 200 J over 10 seconds, what is average power?
questions.why: Divide energy transferred by elapsed time.

questions.clue: Which quantity remains conserved in an isolated collision?
wrong: All kinetic energy in every collision
questions.why: Momentum is conserved even when kinetic energy is not.

questions.clue: A wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
questions.why: Wave speed v=fλ.

questions.clue: Two resistors of 3 Ω and 6 Ω are in series. What is their total resistance?
questions.why: Series resistances add.

questions.clue: Which design approach best isolates the cause of bridge failure?
questions.answer: Change one structural feature per test and record loads
wrong: Use different loads without recording them
questions.why: Controlled trials reveal how individual variables affect performance.

questions.clue: Which ancient civilization developed cuneiform writing?
questions.why: Cuneiform originated in ancient Mesopotamia.

questions.clue: What is a constitutional democracy?
questions.answer: A democracy governed under constitutional limits
questions.why: Constitutional principles limit government authority.

questions.clue: Where did the Renaissance begin as a major cultural movement?
questions.why: The European Renaissance began prominently in Italian centers.

questions.clue: What was a major long-term impact of the printing press in Europe?
wrong: The end of all oral communication
questions.why: Printing expanded reproduction of texts.

questions.clue: Which document limited English royal power in 1215?
questions.why: Magna Carta constrained the king and shaped later legal traditions.

questions.clue: Why do historians use geographic maps?
questions.answer: To study spatial relationships and change
questions.why: Maps show the geographic dimensions of events.

questions.clue: Which 18th-century movement emphasized reason and debate about government?
questions.why: Enlightenment writers debated reason and political authority.

questions.clue: What event is commonly used to mark the start of World War I in 1914?
questions.why: The assassination triggered a diplomatic crisis leading to war.

questions.clue: Which global conflict ended in 1945?
questions.why: Axis powers were defeated in 1945.

questions.clue: What was a central purpose of the United Nations when founded in 1945?
questions.why: The UN was created to support collective peace and cooperation.

questions.clue: Which policy describes European powers controlling overseas colonies for economic and political aims?
questions.why: Imperialism involves extending control over other territories.

questions.clue: Why is corroboration important when studying a historical source?
questions.answer: Other evidence can support or challenge an account
wrong: A single source becomes automatically certain
questions.why: Corroboration checks claims against independent evidence.

questions.clue: Which process describes the end of colonial rule and creation of independent states?
questions.why: Many colonies gained independence after World War II.

questions.clue: What principle requires government powers to be exercised under established law?
questions.why: Rule of law subjects authorities to legal constraints.

questions.clue: Which method best distinguishes correlation from causation in historical analysis?
questions.answer: Assess mechanisms, timelines, and alternative explanations
wrong: Assume simultaneous events always cause each other
questions.why: Causal claims need contextual evidence beyond timing.

questions.clue: What is a metaphor?
questions.why: Metaphor identifies one thing in terms of another.

questions.clue: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet?
questions.why: Shakespeare wrote the tragedy.

questions.clue: What does a narrator do in a story?
questions.answer: Relates the events of the story
questions.why: A narrator provides the narrative voice.

questions.clue: What is dramatic irony?
questions.answer: The audience knows something a character does not
wrong: Every character knows the same information
questions.why: Dramatic irony involves unequal knowledge.

questions.clue: What type of word modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb?
questions.why: Adverbs modify actions or qualities.

questions.clue: Who wrote the novel Frankenstein?
questions.why: Mary Shelley published Frankenstein in 1818.

questions.clue: What is the central conflict in a narrative?
questions.answer: The main struggle driving the plot
questions.why: Conflict creates narrative tension.

questions.clue: What does a thesis statement generally do in an essay?
questions.answer: State the central argument or claim
questions.why: A thesis guides an essay's reasoning.

questions.clue: Which type of evidence best supports a literary interpretation?
wrong: A plot detail unrelated to the claim
questions.why: Textual evidence and analysis support interpretation.

questions.clue: What is an unreliable narrator?
questions.answer: A storyteller whose account should be questioned
questions.why: Narrators may be limited, deceptive, or mistaken.

questions.clue: What is enjambment in poetry?
questions.answer: A sentence or phrase continues past a line break
wrong: Every line ends in a period
questions.why: Enjambment carries syntax beyond a line ending.

questions.clue: Which fallacy attacks a person rather than their argument?
questions.why: Ad hominem targets the speaker instead of the claim.

questions.clue: What is the purpose of a counterargument in persuasive writing?
questions.why: Responding to counterarguments strengthens reasoning.

questions.clue: How does motif differ from a theme?
questions.answer: A motif recurs; a theme is a broader idea or message
wrong: A motif is always the title
A theme is always one repeated object
questions.why: Motifs can reinforce thematic meanings.

questions.clue: Which approach most improves research source evaluation?
questions.answer: Compare authority, evidence, relevance, and potential bias
wrong: Count only the number of images
questions.why: Source evaluation considers provenance and support.

questions.clue: What does a budget compare?
questions.why: Budgets help plan resources and spending.

questions.clue: What does 'interest' generally mean on a savings account?
questions.answer: Money earned based on the deposited balance
wrong: A required tax on every purchase
questions.why: Interest may be paid by a bank on deposits.

questions.clue: What is the median of 2, 5, and 10?
questions.why: The ordered middle value is 5.

questions.clue: What is simple interest on $1,000 at 5% for one year?
What happens to a price after a 20% increase from $50?
questions.why: Twenty percent of 50 is 10.

questions.clue: Which graph best shows change over time?
questions.why: Line graphs make time trends easier to see.

questions.clue: What is the mean of 12, 18, 20, and 30?
questions.why: The sum 80 divided by 4 is 20.

questions.clue: If prices rise generally, what happens to a fixed amount of money's purchasing power?
questions.why: Inflation reduces purchasing power of fixed cash.

questions.clue: How is net income related to gross income?
questions.why: Net pay reflects deductions from gross pay.

questions.clue: Which savings method grows interest on previously earned interest?
questions.why: Compounding earns interest on accumulated interest.

questions.clue: What is the opportunity cost of a decision?
questions.answer: Value of the next-best option forgone
questions.why: Opportunity cost reflects the alternative given up.

questions.clue: What does a high-interest debt generally do compared with low-interest debt?
questions.answer: Costs more to carry, all else equal
questions.why: Higher interest increases financing cost.

questions.clue: If an investment rises from $200 to $230, what is its percentage gain?
questions.why: The $30 increase divided by $200 is 15%.

questions.clue: Why can sampling bias distort survey results?
questions.answer: Some groups may be over- or underrepresented
questions.why: A biased sample can misrepresent the population.

questions.clue: What is a key advantage of diversification?
questions.why: Diversification can reduce concentration risk but not all risk.
